question.prompt: What is the tens digit in the sum \(7! + 8! + 9! + \cdots + 2006!\,?\)

solutions.explanation:
Adding a multiple of \(100\) changes neither the tens digit nor the ones digit, so we only need the last two digits of each term.

Recall that \(n!=1\cdot2\cdots n\). For every \(n\ge10\), this product contains the distinct factors \(2,5,10\), whose product is \(100\). Thus every term from \(10!\) through \(2006!\) is a multiple of \(100\) and does not affect the requested digit.

The remaining terms are
\[
7!=5040,\qquad 8!=40320,\qquad 9!=362880.
\]
Their last two digits contribute
\[
40+20+80=140.
\]
Therefore the complete sum ends in \(40\), and its tens digit is \(\boxed{4}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Keep only the last two digits
